region.name: Payments Incidents And Reliability
region.summary: Engineering incident, postmortem and operational reliability material for the fintech platform, covering the Sep 26 duplicate round-up debits, the Plaid token refresh near-miss, Pillar ACH handling, incident response and notification obligations, plus related diligence prep, MDM rollout gaps and push notification architecture.

brief.text:
This region holds the engineering incident, postmortem and operational reliability record for the fintech platform's money-movement stack. Its anchor is the Sep 26 SEV1 duplicate round-up debit incident, in which the Rails/Sidekiq RoundupSweepJob debited 1,412 users twice for a total of $12,708. The sweep runs daily at 05:30 PT in batches of 250 users. Each batch calls Pillar Bank's transfers API for same-day ACH and then writes roundup_debits to Postgres. The HTTP call and the database write cannot share a transaction, and that gap is the root cause. The timeline runs as follows. A Sep 24 Sidekiq retry config change came first. On Sep 26 a Pillar API latency spike caused client timeouts, and the jobs retried without idempotency keys. A reconciliation alert detected the problem, a SEV1 was declared, and the roundups.sweep_enabled kill switch was flipped. Customer comms, reversals and notification to Pillar Bank followed. The fixes are captured in ADR-031/032. Missing idempotency on money-moving jobs remains an open risk owned by Marcus Bell. A batch control total mismatch is defined as a SEV1. The earlier April 6 ACH pipeline failure is the other major postmortem in this region. It explains why money movement is held to a stricter bar, and it drove the rebuild of the ACH pipeline in Go using an outbox pattern.

The region also covers a near-miss and the operational runbooks. The Plaid access token refresh near-miss was a bug live for about 4 months that left old tokens valid in roughly 0.3% of refreshes. It caused no actual impact. However, if Plaid had enforced one token per user, it could have triggered a P0 cascade of bank-linking auth failures. Marcus Bell found it, Maya Chen reviewed it, and it is classified as a 'loaded gun' bug. The Pillar ACH runbook covers files that get no acknowledgment. After 20 minutes the file is auto re-submitted, and after 40 minutes the issue is escalated. Operators must not use a new file modifier, because doing so risks duplicate debits. The runbook also includes a table of common Pillar reject reasons with their usual causes and actions, and it accounts for the holiday calendar. The incident response framework defines a severity model and six phases: detect, triage, contain, eradicate, notify and review. It also includes a notification obligations table covering Pillar Bank, DriveWealth, customers, regulators, the board and the cyber insurer. As of 2026-10-02, Pillar's 24-hour notification rule explicitly covers operational incidents affecting customer funds, such as the Sep 26 duplicate debits.

Adjacent material includes diligence prep for the Elena Sorensen call. That prep covers 151k MAU, with the Postgres primary expected to break first at 10x scale. It also covers the April 6 and Sep 26 incidents, reconciliation drift in the investing beta, SOC 2 Type II readiness gaps, and key-person risk tied to the VP Eng search. Renee Alvarez owns an open risk that the investing go/no-go is expected to be NO-GO. The MDM rollout left three devices unenrolled with no exceptions granted. Two are Linux engineering workstations covered instead by an endpoint agent plus a script-enforced baseline, and one is the laptop of an employee on leave until Oct 14. The lessons learned were that enrollment effort was underestimated and that the first rollout email looked like phishing. The push notification architecture splits providers: Branch handles transactional pushes and Customer.io handles marketing pushes. A thin Go abstraction service routes by template_key and enforces limits of 3 marketing pushes per day, transactional debounce, quiet hours and a global opt-out. Marcus's team is building it in about 6 weeks. There is also an open todo requiring interview scorecards to cite 2-3 specific moments. Typical questions for this region include what caused the duplicate debits and how much they cost, who must be notified within 24 hours, how to handle an unacknowledged Pillar ACH file, what the Plaid near-miss was, and which reliability risks remain open.
